We have to make it ourselves, says Tajuddin
2021-08-29T00:00:00+06:00 | Shamsuddoza Sajen
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/we-have-make-it-ourselves-says-tajuddin-2163306

August 29, 1971

JANMABHUMI'S PUBLICATION RESUMED

Tajuddin Ahmed, prime minister of Bangladesh, said at Mujibnagar today, "None can bring us freedom. We have to achieve it ourselves by shedding our blood."

Tajuddin Ahmed, who was inaugurating the function organised in connection with the resumption of publication of Janmabhumi, a weekly, said, "No barbarous force can throttle the voice of the people. The republication of Janmabhumi has proved this truth."

The function was attended by many including journalists and writers. Syed Nazrul Islam, the acting president of Bangladesh in a greeting said, "The republication of Janmabhumi at this juncture has created a new chapter in the struggle of Bangladesh."

Mustafa Allama, editor of the weekly said in his address, "We shall create global public opinion in regard to the release of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and recognition of Bangladesh through the paper."

ON THE FRONTLINES

Mukti Bahini today raided Razakars guarding RCC road bridge in Badiakhali area in Mymensingh. Four Rajakars were killed and seven wounded. Another group of freedom fighters damaged a railway bridge near Boira under Sarishabari Police Station with an explosive substance.

In Sylhet, Bangladeshi guerrillas raided the Pakistan troop position in Kamarsail and injured five Pakistani soldiers.

Mukti Bahini ambushed a Pakistani patrol today near Rajshahi and killed six.

5 MILLION AFFECTED IN BANGLADESH

Monsoon floods damaged crops worth about 500 million rupees in Bangladesh. More than five million people were affected by the floods in six districts. The crop damage aggravated existing food shortage.
